I was unable to produce the requested counts because the raw best‑track data (NOAA HURDAT2) is available as a large plain‑text file (e.g., `hurdat2-nepac-1949-2024-031725.txt` – https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-nepac-1949-2024-031725.txt) but no pre‑compiled, decade‑resolved summary of “hurricanes that were within 60 nm of the Mexican coast” exists on the web, and the text file must be parsed and filtered to generate the figures.  No source provides a ready‑made list of:

* the number of Pacific hurricanes that originated off the west coast of Mexico per decade (1990‑1999, 2000‑2009, 2010‑2019),  
* the number of Atlantic hurricanes that originated off the east (Gulf) coast of Mexico per decade,  
* the difference between those numbers for each decade, or  
* a list of Category 4 storms that came within 60 nm of either coast during the decade with the largest difference.

Sources that confirm the availability of the raw data but do not contain the derived counts:

* NOAA HURDAT2 NE/NC Pacific‐Basin file (contains track points for every storm in the eastern Pacific): https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-nepac-1949-2024-031725.txt (Reference: “EP011949 … 7 … 1949‐06‐11 … 20.2N 106.3W 45 …” as shown in the file).  
* NOAA data index page listing the HURDAT files: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/  
* Wikipedia “List of Pacific hurricane records” (mentions NOAA HURDAT2 but no decade‑by‑decade counts): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records.

Because the necessary aggregated counts and the list of Category 4 storms have not been extracted or published in a source I could access, I cannot identify which decade has the largest difference between west‑ and east‑coast origins, nor can I provide the alphabetic list of Category 4 hurricanes within 60 nm of either coast for that decade.
